description: Divulgación científica rural en la ciudad de Latacunga y toda la provincia de Cotopaxi en Ecuador. Utilizo juguetes y materiales reciclados para enseñar lúdicamente física teórica, astrofísica, cosmología y agrofísica a todas las edades, desde niños hasta adultos mayores. Mi proyecto democratiza el acceso a la ciencia al comunicar de forma interactiva los descubrimientos históricos y recientes más impactantes de la NASA.
summary: Leading rural science outreach across Latacunga and the entire Cotopaxi province in Ecuador, I use recycled materials and toys to playfully teach physics, theoretical astrophysics, cosmology, and agrophysics to audiences of all ages—from children and local adults to mayors. My project democratizes access to science by bringing NASA’s groundbreaking historical and recent discoveries directly to rural communities.
details:
What it does & How it works:
My project brings NASA’s historical and recent space missions to life through hands-on, playful storytelling using recycled materials and repurposed toys. Designed specifically for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, I build physical, low-cost scale models of NASA’s iconic rovers, landers, and space probes currently resting on the Moon and Mars. Through interactive rural workshops across Latacunga and the Cotopaxi province in Ecuador, I use these models to explain complex concepts in physics, theoretical astrophysics, cosmology, and agrophysics, transforming discarded Earth materials into vessels of space history.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
By eliminating the need for expensive technology or internet access, my project democratizes science education in underserved rural communities. It bridges the knowledge gap across all generations—engaging everyone from young children and local farmers to community leaders and mayors. My intended impact is to spark scientific curiosity, promote environmental awareness through upcycling, and inspire rural youth in Ecuador to see themselves as future scientists and space explorers.

Tools, Hardware & Software Used:
Instead of traditional high-cost digital hardware or complex coding languages, my primary "hardware" consists of upcycled household plastics, cardboard, electronic scrap, and repurposed toys combined with basic hand tools. For scientific accuracy and storytelling structure, I utilized official NASA open-data portals—including the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), the NASA Science Missions Archive, and NASA Space Place—alongside digital presentation and design software to organize my educational guides.

Creativity & Considerations:
My creativity lies in connecting two seemingly opposite worlds: discarded everyday waste on Earth and NASA’s pioneering hardware "left behind" on other worlds. By giving trash a second life to tell the stories of NASA’s retired explorers, I create a powerful visual metaphor for sustainability and scientific legacy. When designing the experience, I carefully considered local accessibility, cultural relevance, zero-cost scalability, and age-inclusive pedagogy so that any rural community can replicate the project without financial barriers.
